purpose: Every shape Conduit invented where no ground truth existed, and the exact evidence that would displace it. This exists because the repository reversed a standing rule: it used to refuse a feature it could not ground, and now it builds one on an educated guess instead. That reversal is only safe if an invention stays distinguishable from a recovery for as long as it lives, and if the arrival of real evidence is an obligation to reimplement rather than an invitation to feel vindicated.
howThisIsEnforced: scripts/verify-conduit-inventions.mjs checks both directions: every CONDUIT-INVENTED marker in the source is registered here, and every entry here still exists in the source. A marker without a Displaced-by line fails. An entry whose displacement evidence has landed fails, which is the point -- the gate turns 'we should revisit this' into a build failure.

markerConvention.inSource: // CONDUIT-INVENTED: <id>\n// Displaced-by: <the capture or document that would settle it>
markerConvention.note: The id is <context>.<Symbol>. It is not a package path, so moving a file does not silently unregister an invention -- renaming the symbol does, which is when someone should be looking at this anyway.

displacementProcedure: When the named evidence lands, record it under docs/evidence/ or docs/reference-platform/ as a normal capture first. An invention displaced by nothing citable is just a different guess.

Reimplement against the evidence. Do not adapt the invented shape to fit -- the invented shape was chosen without constraint and will bend into agreement, which is how a guess becomes an unfalsifiable claim.
Delete the CONDUIT-INVENTED marker and this entry in the same change as the reimplementation, so the register never describes code that no longer exists.
State in the change what the invention got wrong. That is the only feedback anyone gets about how good these guesses are, and without it the next invention is made no better informed than this one.

inventions.what: The local Grype report envelope retains provider/package/fix data, selects NVD identifiers and scores, and marks normalization as CONDUIT_NATIVE rather than a Hub artifact assessment.
inventions.why: The pinned public CLI page specifies local execution, NVD preference, CVSS v3/v2 fallback, JSON file output and nonzero-exit behavior, but provides no JSON report fixture or complete tie-break rules. Conduit preserves the Grype envelope with explicit native metadata. NVD scores take priority, then version 3 over 2, then highest score and lexical identifier; zero v3 scores use Grype's Negligible label. Only selected v3 scores remain in the primary CVSS array.
inventions.displacedBy: A sanitized Apollo CLI Grype JSON report establishing output schema, normalization tie-breaks and zero-score severity vocabulary.
inventions.riskIfWrong: The local JSON representation may differ from Apollo's. It is marked native, does not fetch Apollo data, and cannot become an authoritative Hub artifact assessment merely by being produced. The Hub scanner's strict immutable-artifact contract is unchanged.

inventions.what: Apollo-shaped resource identifiers for resources Apollo has published no type token for, minted under ri.conduit.main.<type>.<locator> rather than ri.apollo.
inventions.why: The grammar ri.<service>.main.<type>.<locator> is published, and the service segment names the service that owns the resource -- which is why Autopilot's teams are ri.autopilot and not ri.apollo. A Product that exists only in Conduit is owned by Conduit. Guessing a token inside ri.apollo instead would risk a silent collision: if Apollo's real token for something else matches the guess, two different objects share one identifier and nothing raises a hand. A Conduit-namespaced identifier can only be wrong in the direction of being obviously ours. ADR 0007 left this choice open and this is the answer.
inventions.displacedBy: A published statement giving Apollo's own type tokens for Product, Product Release or Bundle resource identifiers.
inventions.riskIfWrong: Low. The identifiers are opaque, self-consistent and unmistakably Conduit's, and every coordinate serving one discloses valueTier: CONDUIT_NATIVE. If Apollo's real tokens arrive, the values change but nothing was ever claimed to match them.

inventions.what: The locator segment of every Apollo resource identifier Conduit mints: the first 12 bytes of a SHA-256 over a stable input, hex encoded.
inventions.why: The grammar around it is published, not invented -- the pinned OpenAPI carries ri.apollo.main.environment.123, ri.apollo.main.installation.123 and ri.apollo.main.package.123, and ri.autopilot.main.team.123 shows the service segment naming the owning service. Only the locator is open, because Apollo's examples use the placeholder 123. A digest rather than a UUID because the value has to be stable across restarts and replicas without being stored; the one Apollo locator whose format is documented, a Plan's, is a UUID, so this is a known divergence rather than an unconstrained choice.
inventions.displacedBy: A published statement of Apollo's RID locator format, for any resource type Conduit holds.
inventions.riskIfWrong: Low in shape, moderate in consequence. The identifiers are opaque and self-consistent, so nothing inside Conduit breaks; but a client that round-trips one into a real Apollo API will not match anything, which is exactly why the coordinates serving them disclose valueTier: CONDUIT_NATIVE.

inventions.what: The optionality Conduit answers for a Product dependency no publisher declared one for: false, rendered as the string "false".
inventions.why: Neither pinned publish request model carries an optionality input -- PublishHelmChartRequest and PublishServiceRequest both stop at extensions -- so a dependency published on the public Apollo routes arrives with nobody having stated whether it is optional. Conduit's own manifest route can state it, and does, but both paths land in catalog.Dependency.Optional, a plain bool: a declared false and an undeclared one are the same stored value, so the read cannot tell them apart. False is the choice because it is the conservative one for a dependency resolver -- treating an unstated dependency as required refuses a Plan that is missing it, where treating it as optional would silently install without it.
inventions.displacedBy: A published Apollo publish request model carrying dependency optionality, which would let a publisher state it and make the served value theirs rather than Conduit's; or, short of that, a tri-state on catalog.Dependency that keeps an undeclared optionality distinguishable from a declared false all the way to the read.
inventions.riskIfWrong: Low. The value is conservative in the direction that fails loudly, and the coordinate discloses valueTier: CONDUIT_NATIVE so a client is told the answer is Conduit's. A dependency a publisher meant as optional reads as required, which blocks a Plan rather than shipping a broken one.

inventions.what: A per-recipient inbox record carrying its own read state.
inventions.why: Read state is modelled per-recipient because two people notified about the same promotion failure read it independently, and storing readAt on the event would let one of them mark it read for both. Apollo has an inbox -- Hub Settings carries a 'My notifications' page and the tenant viewer role names it -- but no capture shows an entry or its read state.
inventions.displacedBy: A capture of Apollo's notification inbox entry and its read state, in particular whether read state is per-recipient.
inventions.riskIfWrong: Medium. Wrong here means the inbox behaves differently from Apollo's, which is visible to operators but not corrupting.

inventions.what: Resolution of one event to its recipients, deduplicated per owner and channel.
inventions.why: Deduplication is a judgement, not a recovery: being told the same thing twice in the same place teaches people to ignore it. The channel half of the key is grounded -- Apollo configures email and in-app independently, so reaching one person on both is intended -- but collapsing one owner reached by two preferences on one channel is Conduit's own choice, and Apollo may well fan out per preference instead.
inventions.displacedBy: A capture of how Apollo resolves one event to its recipients, in particular whether it deduplicates a recipient reached by two preferences.
inventions.riskIfWrong: Low. Changing the fan-out rule changes delivery volume, not stored shape.

inventions.what: The rendered form of one inbox entry that a delivery transport sends: a subject line built from the event type and environment, a body of the emitter's summary followed by the event id, type, resource, environment, actor and time, and the destination the recipient's own contact resolved to, which is absent when they hold none.
inventions.why: Something has to decide the wording, and deciding it once in the domain is better than deciding it per adapter, where two transports would phrase the same failure differently and give an operator two facts to reconcile during an incident. Apollo's settings pages establish that email and Slack contacts receive notifications; no capture shows what the message looks like when it arrives, so every choice here -- that the subject leads with the type a subscriber filtered on, that the body repeats the identifiers needed to act without opening a console -- is Conduit's.
inventions.displacedBy: a capture of what Apollo puts in a notification email or Slack post, in particular whether the subject names the event type or the resource
inventions.riskIfWrong: Low and cosmetic in the near term: a wrong subject line is annoying rather than dangerous. It becomes expensive if anyone parses the body, because a downstream receiver built against this shape has to change when the real one arrives. That is why the webhook payload is versioned and structured rather than only textual.

inventions.what: The JSON body Conduit POSTs when delivering a notification to a configured webhook endpoint: a version discriminator, the event and recipient identity the delivery is keyed on, the rendered subject and body, a Slack-compatible text field, and an optional destination object naming the kind and address the recipient's own contact resolved to.
inventions.why: A transport had to exist for the readiness document's Tier 1 gap 1 to close, and a webhook is the one transport Conduit can honestly offer: SMTP needs a recipient address and no store in this repository holds one. Apollo establishes that a team may own a Slack contact and that Slack contacts are deliverable; nothing establishes the request Apollo makes, so the field names, the version discriminator and the decision to duplicate the body into a Slack-shaped text field are Conduit's own.
inventions.displacedBy: a capture of the request Apollo makes when it delivers to a Slack or email team contact, including its field names and headers
inventions.riskIfWrong: Moderate, because this one is on the wire. A receiver written against these field names has to change when the observed request arrives, and a deployment that has pointed a mail relay at this endpoint would keep delivering under the old shape until it did. The version discriminator exists so that change is detectable rather than silent.

inventions.what: The Hub's authenticated notification routes and their request and response shapes: GET /v1/notifications/inbox, GET /v1/notifications/events, GET and PUT /v1/notifications/preferences keyed on the (resource, owner, channel) tuple the store already holds one row for, and GET, PUT and DELETE /v1/notifications/contacts keyed on the (owner, kind) tuple the address book holds one row for.
inventions.why: The pinned Apollo OpenAPI under docs/reference-platform/snapshots/ publishes no notification operation -- the string does not occur in api-definition.yml -- so there was no published shape to be faithful to. The settings pages captured in docs/evidence/apollo-notification-types.json establish the grain being edited (a per-resource, per-channel preference list, For User or For Team) and nothing else about a wire format, so the routes carry that grain and invent only the spelling. Declining to build it was the alternative, and it leaves the Tier 1 readiness gap open: a preference editable only through the store is not editable.
inventions.displacedBy: A capture of Apollo's notification Hub API -- its route paths, its request and response shapes, and how it scopes an inbox read to a caller.
inventions.riskIfWrong: Low outside Conduit, moderate inside it. Nothing round-trips these shapes into Apollo, and the routes sit under /v1/notifications where no Apollo-shaped route lives, so a wrong guess cannot collide with a real operation. What a wrong guess costs is a console and any client written against it, which would have to be rewritten when the real shape arrives.

inventions.what: A stored destination per (owner, kind) -- an address, its kind, an opt-into-future-resources flag and its timestamps -- where the owner may be a TEAM or a USER, and an identifier minted as a digest over (owner, kind) rather than chosen or derived from the address.
inventions.why: Apollo establishes the team half: a contact is created in Hub Settings, has one of three kinds, is what a resource selects, and a team holding none receives nothing. It establishes no user contact at all, and may well have none -- a tenant's account email would do the same job. Conduit needs one anyway, because its preference model already admits a USER owner on the EMAIL channel and without an address that subscription reaches nobody, which is precisely the Tier 1 readiness gap this closes. Keying on (owner, kind) rather than on a contact identifier follows the dialog, which creates a contact of a kind for an owner; the identifier is derived from the same tuple so every replica mints it without storing it, and deliberately not from the address, because an identifier derived from an address carries the address wherever it travels and changes identity when somebody moves.
inventions.displacedBy: A capture of Apollo's contact API -- what a contact is keyed on, whether a user holds one at all, what it is called, and what its identifier looks like.
inventions.riskIfWrong: Moderate, and the highest-consequence entry in this register, because the value stored is personal data. Being wrong about the shape costs a migration. Being wrong about the authorization would cost somebody their mail, which is why the owner check admits no administrator override and is held down by TestThroughTheHubOnePrincipalCannotWriteAnotherPrincipalsContact rather than by this paragraph. A user contact that Apollo turns out not to have is a table Conduit stops writing, not a value anyone round-trips into Apollo.

inventions.what: The rule that turns one recipient into one destination at delivery time: skip contacts belonging to another owner, skip an in-app recipient entirely, skip any kind Apollo does not deliver to, prefer the kind whose name matches the channel, break remaining ties by kind name, and resolve to nothing when no contact qualifies -- which leaves the operator-configured endpoint as the fallback.
inventions.why: Something has to choose, because Apollo publishes two per-resource channels (EMAIL, IN_APP) and three contact kinds (EMAIL, SLACK, PAGERDUTY), and the two vocabularies overlap in exactly one place. What is grounded: PagerDuty receives nothing, so it is never a destination; an in-app entry is delivered by the inbox, so an address would send it somewhere its owner never chose. What is Conduit's: that a team whose only contact is Slack is reached there rather than not at all, that ties break by kind name so two replicas resolving at the same moment agree, and that a recipient with no contact falls back rather than failing. A failed read of the address book is deliberately not folded into 'no contact' -- that retries, because delivering to the fallback on a failed query would send a person's notification somewhere they did not choose.
inventions.displacedBy: A capture of how Apollo chooses which of a recipient's contacts a notification is delivered to, and what it does when the recipient has none.
inventions.riskIfWrong: Moderate. Wrong here changes where a notification lands rather than what is stored, and the fallback bounds the worst case at the behaviour that existed before contacts: a deployment that records no contacts is bit-for-bit unchanged. The direction that would cost most is preferring a kind Apollo would not have, which is why the kind is on the wire beside the address so a receiver can refuse one it does not expect.

inventions.what: Which of Apollo's two observed recall notification event types Conduit raises for a given recall: PRODUCT_IN_OPEN_ENDED_RECALL when the recall has no ending version and is not single-version, and PRODUCT_RECALLS otherwise.
inventions.why: Both labels are observed, in docs/evidence/apollo-notification-types.json, and so are their descriptions -- 'Future releases of this Product will be recalled' for the first, 'Anytime a bug or critical issue has been discovered in my product' for the second. A Conduit recall with no upper bound covers every version the Product will ever publish above its starting version, which is the first description exactly. What is not established is that Apollo distributes the two this way: the same capture records, as an upstream ambiguity, that nothing says whether these are two types or one type rendered at two granularities. Raising only one of them was the alternative, and it would have told a subscriber who ticked the other that no recall had opened.
inventions.displacedBy: a capture showing which notification event type Apollo raises for a recall with an ending version, against one without
inventions.riskIfWrong: Low, and reversible in one function. Nothing leaves Conduit under these type names except a notification a Conduit deployment delivers to its own configured transport, and both names are Apollo's own, so a wrong split mislabels an inbox row rather than inventing a vocabulary. What it costs is a subscriber who ticked exactly one of the two: they see the recalls Conduit routed to their type and not the others, which reads as no recall having opened.

inventions.what: A `facets` object on GET /v1/fleet/installations counting installations per value of environment, product, health, rolloutStatus, configStatus and lifecycle, where each dimension's count is computed with that dimension's own filter excluded from the query.
inventions.why: The console needed a faceted filter rail, and the Hub already served per-dimension counts as `summary`. `summary` is computed after the whole query is applied, so once health=UNHEALTHY is selected every other health bucket reads zero -- a control that says "HEALTHY 0" beside a fleet that is mostly healthy. Excluding a dimension from its own facet is the conventional resolution and the only one under which the number beside a filter answers the question the click asks: how many rows would I get if I picked this instead. The alternative considered was serving `summary` unchanged and labelling the rail "within the current selection", which needs no invention and was rejected because it makes the rail unusable for navigation -- every unselected sibling reads zero, so there is nothing to navigate to. What is NOT established is that Apollo serves such a shape at all: the pinned OpenAPI snapshot publishes no fleet-installation filter-count operation, and the 2020 screenshot in docs/ui/evidence/legacy-apollo-2020/ shows a rail with counts and proportional bars without showing what the counts are computed over. The key names are Conduit's own query parameters, deliberately, so that a facet cannot be served under a name the filter would not accept.
inventions.displacedBy: a capture or published schema showing Apollo's own fleet/installation filter-count response -- its field names, and whether a selected dimension is excluded from its own count
inventions.riskIfWrong: Low and reversible in one function plus one console component. Nothing leaves Conduit under this shape except the console's own read of its own Hub; the surrounding `summary`, `installations` and pagination fields are untouched, so a client that ignores `facets` is unaffected. The failure mode if the exclusion semantics are wrong is a rail whose counts do not match the result an operator then gets, which the rail's own labelling addresses by stating what each count is over. Authorization is not at risk: facet contributions pass the same per-Environment read check as rows, so no count discloses an Environment the caller may not read.

inventions.what: The scan-freshness window an ArtifactSecurityPolicy enforces when it states none: seven days, applied as a floor rather than as an off switch, so a policy requiring PASS can no longer accept evidence of unbounded age.
inventions.why: That freshness was optional was the residue #54 named, and closing it required choosing a number nothing establishes. What is grounded is the direction, not the value: Apollo's own material describes continuous rescanning that catches vulnerabilities discovered after a Release passed, which only means anything if a passing scan expires. Seven days was chosen for the shape of its failure modes rather than for any evidence -- exceeding it costs a rescan wherever a scanner is configured, so too tight costs latency while too loose restores the defect. A day was rejected because on a Hub with no scanner configured it fails closed daily, and a floor that reads as breakage gets switched off.
inventions.displacedBy: a published statement of the scan-freshness window Apollo applies when a security constraint names none
inventions.riskIfWrong: Low and bounded by configuration. Wrong here means Conduit rescans on a different cadence from Apollo, which any Environment can correct by stating maximumScanAgeSeconds explicitly; nothing on the wire carries the value and no stored shape depends on it. The one deployment it can disturb is a Hub running a PASS policy with no scanner and evidence older than a week, which is refused where it was previously admitted -- intended, and the reason the number is not tighter.

inventions.what: A Conduit-native append-only promotion run with RUNNING, SUCCEEDED, ABORTED and CANCELLED phases, exact predecessor continuation and a durable terminal reason, separate from PASSED/BLOCKED eligibility.
inventions.why: The pinned public release-channel documentation and changelog establish in-progress, succeeded and aborted promotions and cancellation reasons, but publish no lifecycle API shape or transition contract. Keeping immutable evaluations in a predecessor chain preserves existing eligibility replay and provides atomic terminal transitions without rewriting prior decisions.
inventions.displacedBy: A published Apollo promotion lifecycle API schema and transition contract, including cancellation reasons.
inventions.riskIfWrong: Medium. Run identifiers, phase wire tokens and continuation requests may differ from Apollo. They are served only on Conduit-native v1 routes with CONDUIT_NATIVE disclosure; published Apollo transport schemas remain unchanged.

inventions.what: A first-class SLACK channel for native v1 resource preferences, inbox fan-out and channel-specific delivery.
inventions.why: Public notifications documentation establishes Slack delivery and captured team contacts establish the Slack destination kind, but the captured resource settings only show email and in-app preference lists. The maintainer requested native multi-channel delivery in #119. A separate channel makes routing explicit without claiming a recovered private preference schema.
inventions.displacedBy: A published or authorized captured Apollo per-resource Slack notification preference schema.
inventions.riskIfWrong: Low for native delivery, moderate for compatibility claims. The channel and its subscription scope are Conduit-owned; published Apollo transports remain unchanged. Future recovered preference schemas require reimplementation against that evidence.

inventions.what: Conduit-owned persisted Space identity and grouping metadata, including a random space_ identifier, immutable Environment/Product/Bundle anchor assignments, creation provenance and explicit native tier.
inventions.why: The adopted decision in #17 requires a real first-class grouping. Public CLI references and the Rosetta release notes establish Space selection and guest-user publication, while apollo-identifier-grammar.json distinguishes externally issued Apollo Space identity from Foundry namespace identity. These sources do not establish a native Hub Space record, identifier format, or ownership transport. This model supplies native persisted data without claiming to issue an Apollo identity or confer resource grants.
inventions.displacedBy: A sanitized Apollo Space record establishing identity, grouping metadata and ownership semantics, including guest-user publication.
inventions.riskIfWrong: The native identity, record schema, and immutable anchor assignment policy require an explicit migration if recovered evidence differs. Entity and Release grouping derives from their owning Environment and Product; assignment intent does not assert a resource is live. Group selection never grants authorization; existing resource checks remain required. No private Apollo Space transport or role family is claimed.

inventions.what: Conduit-native Space creation/read/list and immutable grouping-assignment routes under /v1/spaces, with typed native records and filtered rosters.
inventions.why: The adopted Space grouping decision requires management of persisted native data. Existing evidence establishes Space selection and the distinction from Foundry namespaces but no private Apollo Space management wire or role family. This surface uses the existing canonical platform/root permission-management authority for creation/assignment and existing per-resource read authority for visibility; it does not fabricate Apollo Space permissions.
inventions.displacedBy: A published or sanitized Apollo Space management API establishing routes, body shapes, visibility and assignment authority.
inventions.riskIfWrong: The native routes and assignment policy require migration if recovered evidence differs. Grouping and selection grant no resource access. Creation subjects come from verified request identity, delegated callers retain their original carrier for authorization, and unrelated resource identities are filtered from rosters.

inventions.what: Native space create/get/list/bind/bindings commands over the typed /v1/spaces management adapter.
inventions.why: The adopted grouping decision needs operators to inspect and assign persisted native Spaces. Captured CLI selection flags do not establish a Space management command group; these commands disclose native scope and use Hub authority rather than local claims.
inventions.displacedBy: A published or sanitized Apollo Space management CLI contract defining command paths, arguments and mutation semantics.
inventions.riskIfWrong: Command spelling and binding workflow may require migration. Native records retain provenance, Hub authorization filters reads and controls mutations, and membership grants no resource permissions.

inventions.what: The five recovered spaceId fields resolve independently authorized persisted native assignments; Entity inherits Environment and Release inherits Product. Native Bundle RID lookup uses the authorized persisted Bundle catalogue and retains the recovered scalar bundles shape.
inventions.why: The adopted #17 decision requires real Space data rather than a default constant. Evidence establishes the five names but not a private Apollo membership source or Bundle lookup implementation. ADR 0014 defines and discloses these bounded native choices.
inventions.displacedBy: A published or sanitized Apollo record establishing Space identity per Environment, Entity, Product, Release and Bundle, plus Bundle lookup semantics.
inventions.riskIfWrong: Membership inheritance and native Bundle identifiers require migration if recovered evidence differs. Read authority remains canonical and carrier-aware; missing assignment is distinct from unavailable or denied storage. All six native values disclose CONDUIT_NATIVE while coordinate provenance remains OBSERVED.

inventions.what: Native spaceId query selection before Environment pagination, optional profile/global CLI selection, and immutable Product grouping reservation before selected native Helm/Terraform publication.
inventions.why: Captured CLI notes establish explicit Space selection and guest use, but not the private transport or native assignment policy. Existing grants remain the resource authority. Conduit has no primary-organization inference: an explicit readable Space and canonical artifact/product/release permissions govern guest publication.
inventions.displacedBy: A published or sanitized Apollo Space selection and publication contract establishing transport, caller access, grouping reservation and failure behavior.
inventions.riskIfWrong: The query transport and reservation policy may require migration. Assignment intent may survive a later failed publication and never asserts an artifact exists. Explicit selection cannot move an immutable existing assignment. Forbidden selection and missing publication authority fail before reservation; store failure is not an empty page.

inventions.what: Offline native preparation of Hub/Spoke Product publication inputs with exact chart/image digests, pinned default image configuration and producer display tags, plus a six-target CLI download-asset declaration.
inventions.why: Issue #193 authorizes preparation without live publication. Conduit owns these Product coordinates and metadata format. Version 2 uses the native download-assets API for CLI archive metadata while keeping CLI Releases non-executable and preserving version-1 inventory evidence as historical preparation.
inventions.displacedBy: an owner-approved self-Product publication contract defining coordinates, artifact inputs and the supported CLI asset catalogue.
inventions.riskIfWrong: Product naming and preparation format may need migration before publication. Input metadata consistency and CLI byte hashes do not authenticate signatures or registry availability. Output says NOT_PUBLISHED and preserves those unperformed checks; no publication, subscription or deployment authority is added.

inventions.what: Windows0.148.0 hash-pinned handshake-only preflight; runtime remains unavailable.
inventions.why: Check exact protocol/home boundaries without launching an agent whose host-read confinement has not been established.
inventions.displacedBy: A reviewed, scoped, authenticated agent runtime contract with enforced workspace isolation.
inventions.riskIfWrong: Handshake success says nothing about safe inference, tool confinement or deployment authority; profile reports model disabled.

inventions.what: Unsigned local structural-validator receipt binding exact artifact/tool/schema/script bytes and recording dependency versions and mandatory check outcomes.
inventions.why: Separate actual deterministic tool observations from model prose without inventing release or deployment authority.
inventions.displacedBy: An authenticated validator-producer and freshness contract integrated with existing governance.
inventions.riskIfWrong: JSON receipts can be forged outside their local producer; they must not be ingested as trusted approval or proof of image/runtime readiness.

inventions.what: Versioned source-evidence-bound caller review to constrained scaffold workflow, not delivery approval.
inventions.why: Invalidate stale review inputs and keep unsupported application requirements explicit before artifact emission.
inventions.displacedBy: A reviewed production evidence-to-packaging workflow contract.
inventions.riskIfWrong: Caller declarations can be incorrect; byte-bound evidence is not semantic truth, image provenance, runtime validation or human authorization.

inventions.what: Conduit-native constrained internal-stateless profile emitting deterministic review artifacts, not deployable integration.
inventions.why: Keep unsupported requirements explicit while testing pinned schema contracts before agent runtime integration.
inventions.displacedBy: A reviewed production packaging profile contract.
inventions.riskIfWrong: Schema-valid artifacts can still fail startup, identity, storage, network or offline requirements; no readiness or execution approval is implied.

inventions.what: Conduit-native completeness review of supplied application packaging assessments; never deployment authorization.
inventions.why: Separates missing or inferred evidence from source-cited claims before generating UDS artifacts, without treating a model assertion as validation.
inventions.displacedBy: A reviewed replacement packaging-assessment contract.
inventions.riskIfWrong: Overly narrow checklist may miss requirements; reports explicitly remain unvalidated and do not authorize execution.

inventions.what: When a product does not declare a section, a packaging run emits one OpenID client named for the product with redirect https://<name>.example/callback and secret <name>-sso, egress TCP and UDP 53 to kube-system pods labeled k8s-app=kube-dns, and a monitor named http on the product port at /metrics. Explicit lines replace that section. The word none keeps the section and emits an empty list.
inventions.why: The Package custom resource requires monitor port name, selector and target port, and its network allow list is deny-by-default. No published package profile states what to write when the product is silent. Name resolution is the allow list that does not publish the workload, and the client and monitor names follow the product name so two runs of the same source agree.
inventions.displacedBy: a reviewed packaging profile that states the SSO client, network allow and monitor values to emit when a product declares none.
inventions.riskIfWrong: A product that needed no name resolution, a different client, or no metrics scrape receives those defaults until it declares otherwise. Empty lists are available with none. The output is not deployment authorization, and the value tier annotation says the choice is native.

inventions.what: Immutable native download-asset declarations with stable Product/version coordinates, HTTPS URLs, declared SHA-256 hashes, optional target and evidence coordinates, and server-recorded preparation provenance.
inventions.why: Conduit self-delivery requires a CLI asset catalogue. Existing Helm and Terraform publication bodies do not describe downloadable binaries, and no recovered Apollo contract establishes this shape. Prepared metadata becomes published only through a matching catalogue receipt; it grants no execution or verification authority.
inventions.displacedBy: A published or owner-approved download-asset Product contract establishing manifest shape, catalogue authority and execution eligibility.
inventions.riskIfWrong: The native declaration shape may need replacement. CONDUIT_NATIVE and PUBLISHER_DECLARED distinguish it from recovered contracts and verified artifacts. Storage and application foundations alone expose no route or production publication capability.

inventions.what: Native download-asset publication, release metadata and per-Product release listing routes, optionally composed with an immutable declaration store.
inventions.why: The native download-asset declaration has no recovered public transport. Composition reuses original-carrier publication/resource-read decisions and catalogue receipts without creating executable Release definitions.
inventions.displacedBy: A published or owner-approved download-asset publication API establishing routes, payloads, authority and failure semantics.
inventions.riskIfWrong: Route and document spellings may need replacement. They are native surfaces, not unpublished private interoperability; declared asset URLs and hashes remain unverified, and no Agent execution path is created.

inventions.what: The native product-release download-assets publish/get/list CLI, strict JSON declarations and an offline dry run that does not contact the Hub.
inventions.why: A native asset Product needs an operator path distinct from Helm execution. Existing optional operator transport ports carry the declaration and receipt-bound reads, preserving explicit Space selection on publication.
inventions.displacedBy: A published or owner-approved download-asset CLI contract establishing command paths, declarations, dry-run and catalogue read semantics.
inventions.riskIfWrong: The command grammar may need replacement. Metadata is publisher-declared, native and non-executable; local preparation and dry run grant no Hub publication authority and verify no signatures.

inventions.what: Native append-only discussion records with request-scoped comment IDs, effective author, original carrier, server UTC time and bounded untrimmed text; independently stored and read under existing request visibility.
inventions.why: The reviewed CLI comment page establishes one request argument and required text, not a backing transport or output model. Annotation reuses the existing author/reviewer mutation authority; reading reuses the existing request-read policy. Comments cannot update reviews, approval or Plans. Eight-record cursor pages bound the operator response even for maximal JSON-escaped text.
inventions.displacedBy: A published or sanitized Change Request discussion contract establishing record fields, comment authority, transport routes and pagination semantics.

inventions.what: A native add/remove endpoint and explicit APPLIED/PREVIEW result, using serialized Change Request/Plan updates and the existing author/reviewer label authority.

Newly attached normal names resolve active label-definition IDs; the existing Do not merge tag is built in and attached legacy tags remain removable. Preview computes prospective state without repository or audit writes.

inventions.displacedBy: A published or sanitized CLI discussion/label result contract establishing native-ID projection, preview output and a discussion-list operation.

inventions.what: Structured native batch/preview receipts and partial-failure output for the Experimental temporary Entity maintenance CLI.

displaced.whatTheInventionGotWrong: Its premise. The entry said Conduit 'carries the Environment where Apollo's documented example carries a Space'. Apollo's documented example carries no Space: the pinned OpenAPI publishes aeid:apollo-environment-demo:helm-chart:wordpress twice, beside environmentRid, and that second segment is an environment name. Conduit's aeid:<environment>:helm-chart:<entity> matches the published example in segment count, in the helm-chart product-type token, and in the meaning of the second segment. Nothing was invented; the construction was recovered and then filed as a guess.
displaced.howThisWentWrong: The grammar record's own conduitBearing already said the space-or-environment question was NOT established, and the invention entry -- written after reading it -- asserted it was a Space anyway. That is an inference hardening into a fact across two files in one day. The answer was in a snapshot this repository has held since the OpenAPI was pinned; nobody had compared the OSDK example against the OpenAPI example. The OSDK's 'mojito' says nothing about what it is, which is exactly why it should not have been read as saying 'Space'.
displaced.note: ApolloEntity.id still discloses valueTier: CONDUIT_NATIVE, and that is unchanged and correct: no Apollo Hub answered with the string, Conduit composed it from its own environment and entity names. Serving a value built to a published shape is still serving a value Conduit built.

displaced.whatTheInventionGotWrong: It existed at all. Apollo's notification subscriptions carry no severity: filtering is by type and channel, and nothing on any notification page or screenshot has a severity, priority or urgency control. The invention also named a displacement condition -- 'a capture establishing Apollo's MonitoringSeverity enum members' -- that could never have displaced it, because this repository's own reference note already records MonitoringSeverity as a Foundry Data Health type rather than an Apollo one. An invention whose stated evidence cannot settle it is unfalsifiable, which is the failure the register exists to prevent and which the register itself shipped.
displaced.note: Apollo does have a severity, on the Environment Events surface, where the 2020 capture shows the facet Success/Info/Warning/Error. That is a different surface and is not modelled here. Note also that the invented members -- INFO, WARNING, ACTION_REQUIRED, CRITICAL -- match neither that vocabulary nor its ordering.

displaced.whatTheInventionGotWrong: Every name, and worse, the shape. All eight invented kinds are gone; nine observed types replace them, and not one invented name survived. The structural error was closing the set: Apollo's documentation says the supported types 'will grow over time', and the settings page carries a per-resource, per-channel toggle reading 'If enabled, you will opt into future notification types added for this resource'. Apollo solved openness with forward consent. The invention closed the vocabulary and justified it by analogy to the Change Type taxonomy -- reasoning from a neighbouring design instead of looking, which is exactly how a closed set becomes the thing that silently drops every type added later.

The grain and three whole dimensions. Apollo's unit is a preference per (resource, principal, channel), not one subscription filtered by kind and severity. Missing entirely: delivery channels, team contacts as a prerequisite for a team receiving anything, and the two opt-into-future toggles. Present and wrong: a severity floor Apollo does not have, and a Muted boolean where Apollo's mute vocabulary belongs to monitors. The one part that held was ownership by user or team, which was the one part grounded in recovered evidence rather than guessed.

howThisWentWrong.note: All three displacements landed the day after the register was written, from evidence that was already in reach. This is recorded because the register's value depends on its guesses being honest ones, and these were not -- they were made without looking.
whatWasAvailable: Three public Palantir documentation pages under managing-notifications, already listed in docs/reference-platform/public-documentation-manifest.tsv with their content digests.

Five screenshots on those pages, already counted by docs/reference-platform/IMAGE-DERIVED-GAPS.md, which dispositioned the section 'Boundary' without opening them -- in a document whose own thesis is that screenshots are where a UI-first product states its enum values.
docs/ui/evidence/legacy-apollo-2020/environment-events.webp, committed in this repository, showing the Events severity and category facets.
howThisWentWrong.whyItWasNotSeen: docs/reference-platform/reference/notifications.md opened with 'No public Palantir docs page was captured for this capability'. That sentence was false against this repository's own manifest, had never been checked against it, and was taken at face value. The gate added in scripts/verify-documentation-claims.mjs now checks exactly this class of claim, because it is the cheapest possible check and nothing was doing it.
howThisWentWrong.lesson: The register asks whether an invention is marked and whether it names what would displace it. It does not ask whether the invention was necessary. A guess made without exhausting the sources already in the repository is not an educated guess, and marking it does not make it one.
